item.title: A decade of partnership

item.content:encoded:
THE Foundation for Rural Integrated Enterprises and Development (FRIEND) Fiji has marked a decade of partnership with Motibhai Group of Companies, celebrating a relationship that has helped bring community-sourced, Fijian-made products into homes across the country.

The milestone was celebrated on Wednesday at the Motibhai Building in Walu Bay, Suva, and was officiated by Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica.

The partnership comes as FRIEND marks 25 years of service in Fiji, having started in the aftermath of the 2000 civil unrest to help communities build livelihoods from local skills, knowledge and resources.

FRIEND acting chief executive officer Viloki Gohil said the 10-year partnership demonstrated the impact of genuine corporate social partnerships.

“Over these 10 years, this relationship has shown what genuine corporate social partnership can achieve,” Ms Gohil said.

“Motibhai’s distribution strength has helped connect community-sourced products with wider markets, creating visibility for Fijian-made goods and opportunity for the people behind them.”

She said FRIEND’s work had evolved from helping rural communities develop products to helping them meet the demands of formal markets, including quality control, packaging and distribution.

The organisation has worked with communities to develop locally available root crops, fruits and traditional food preservation skills into flours, dried products and other value-added foods.

Ms Gohil said FRIEND was now entering a new phase focused on market expansion, scalable growth and food innovation.

“As FRIEND steps into its next 25 years, we want to expand what is possible for rural enterprise – greater visibility for local products, stronger opportunities for communities and partnerships that combine commercial capability with social purpose.

“This anniversary is not only a reflection on where we began; it is a commitment to the next chapter.”

The partnership is aimed at strengthening local value chains while creating sustainable income opportunities for rural households, women and young people.

FRIEND stated the collaboration demonstrated how private sector networks and community organisations could work together to support inclusive economic development and reduce reliance on grant funding.

item.title: Weather-ready tourism
item.description: TOURISM stakeholders in Nadi and Denarau are exploring ways to improve how weather forecasts and warnings are used to make decisions affecting guests, staff and tourism activities. Speaking to this newspaper, Dr Rochelle Campbell of the Hydrologic Research Center, NOAA and the US Department of State said the Fiji Tourism Impact-Based Forecasting (IBF) workshop was aimed at helping tourism operator
item.content:encoded:
TOURISM stakeholders in Nadi and Denarau are exploring ways to improve how weather forecasts and warnings are used to make decisions affecting guests, staff and tourism activities.

Speaking to this newspaper, Dr Rochelle Campbell of the Hydrologic Research Center, NOAA and the US Department of State said the Fiji Tourism Impact-Based Forecasting (IBF) workshop was aimed at helping tourism operators use forecast information to support timely decisions.

“Very much today, we are using them as the experts in the room to better understand what the challenges are and what they need to know,” she said.

Dr Campbell said the workshop would also assess whether the forecast information available would meet the needs of tourism operators.

The Hydrologic Research Center, in collaboration with the Fiji Meteorological Service, held a similar workshop in 2024.

The latest workshop aimed to better understand the sector’s specific information needs and help improve the delivery of relevant forecasts.

She said the program focused mainly on Suva and this was the second workshop held in Nadi.

Nadi and Denarau face hazards including heat stress, marine threats, severe weather, lightning, flash flooding and coastal inundation.

These can affect guest safety, staff welfare, transport, business continuity and tourism activities.

The two-day workshop brought together representatives from government, hotels, resorts, marine and dive operators and tourism organisations to strengthen Fiji’s weather-readiness capacity.

item.title: 100-plus groups benefit from grants – Singh
item.description: MORE than 100 religious organisations and communities have benefited from projects supported through the multi-ethnic grant program. Its line minister Charan Jeath Singh said the program continued to support community-based organisations by helping improve facilities and responding to needs at the grassroots level.
item.content:encoded:
MORE than 100 religious organisations and communities have benefited from projects supported through the multi-ethnic grant program.

Its line minister Charan Jeath Singh said the program continued to support community-based organisations by helping improve facilities and responding to needs at the grassroots level.

“The program remains an important mechanism through which Government partners with communities to improve facilities, strengthen community organisations and support social cohesion,” he said.

One of the projects supported under the program was the repair and renovation of the Ranibulu Shree Sanatan Dharam Ganesh Mandir.

The ministry provided $10,912 towards the purchase of materials for the project, while the temple community contributed labour.

He said the temple had suffered termite damage, which weakened the wooden structures and posed potential risks to worshippers and community members.

“The repair and renovation work, therefore addressed not only the appearance of the temple, but also the safety and functionality of an important community facility,” he said.

He said the project demonstrated the importance of Government working together with communities.

“The committee’s contribution of labour is a good example of community ownership and demonstrates that successful Government-supported projects are built on partnership.”

He said they recognised the important role played by mandir, mosques, churches, temples, and other community organisations in bringing people together and strengthening social cohesion.

item.title: Issues delay health centre opening, says Ravunawa
item.description: THE commissioning of the Vuo Health Centre in Labasa has been deferred because of outstanding documentation and paperwork involving key stakeholders. The health centre was expected to be commissioned last month, but the opening did not proceed as planned.
item.content:encoded:
THE commissioning of the Vuo Health Centre in Labasa has been deferred because of outstanding documentation and paperwork involving key stakeholders.

The health centre was expected to be commissioned last month, but the opening did not proceed as planned.

Assistant Health Minister Penioni Ravunawa said land issues and the inclusion of a minor operating theatre were among the major factors behind the deferment.

“There were some documents and paperwork by the Ministry of Lands, the iTaukei Land Trust Board and the inclusion of a minor operating theatre in the building,” Mr Ravunawa said.

Mr Ravunawa said some smaller logistical matters needed to be resolved before the facility could be commissioned.

“These are the major factors apart from some small logistics which the stakeholders are currently working on.

The deferment means residents who were expecting to gain access to the upgraded health services at the facility will have to wait until the outstanding matters are resolved.

He said stakeholders were currently working through the remaining issues.

The inclusion of a minor operating theatre is expected to expand the range of services that can be provided at the facility once it becomes operational.

item.title: Pay lapse after study leave – MP
item.description: A healthcare worker who survived a maritime incident in Lau last month went without salary for at least three months after applying for and being granted study leave, Assistant Health Minister Penioni Ravunawa has confirmed. Mr Ravunawa said the worker, understood to be a peer educator, had initially applied for study leave, which was approved, resulting in the cessation of her salary.
item.content:encoded:
A healthcare worker who survived a maritime incident in Lau last month went without salary for at least three months after applying for and being granted study leave, Assistant Health Minister Penioni Ravunawa has confirmed.

Mr Ravunawa said the worker, understood to be a peer educator, had initially applied for study leave, which was approved, resulting in the cessation of her salary.

“She initially applied for study leave, which was approved, and the cessation of her salary was effective,” he said.

However, the worker later changed her mind and returned to the Ministry of Health.

Mr Ravunawa said the salary lapse occurred because a process under the Government of Fiji Finance Instructions had to be followed when an employee resumed work after approved leave.

“The worker later changed her mind and rejoined the ministry,” he said.

“In such cases, there’s a process to be followed in accordance with the Government of Fiji Finance Instructions. Hence, there was a lapse in her salary.”

He said the worker was eventually placed back on the payroll after the ministry became aware of the situation.

The healthcare worker was among six medical personnel who were stranded at sea for more than 30 hours in Lau waters while travelling for health outreach work.

They were eventually rescued by the crew of the Lomaiviti Princess 12 and taken to Lakeba for medical assessment.

item.title: Interns finally posted
item.description: MEDICAL interns have finally been assigned to hospitals after spending at least six weeks at home, with the Health Ministry attributing the delay to several administrative and clinical requirements. Assistant Health Minister Penioni Ravunawa said the posting process involved a number of factors that had to be resolved before the interns could be deployed.
item.content:encoded:
MEDICAL interns have finally been assigned to hospitals after spending at least six weeks at home, with the Health Ministry attributing the delay to several administrative and clinical requirements.

Assistant Health Minister Penioni Ravunawa said the posting process involved a number of factors that had to be resolved before the interns could be deployed.

He said one of the requirements was the mandatory open merit recruitment and selection process, while some had failed to complete their clinical examination requirements for their logbooks and had to repeat.

“Another factor was the timing of receiving final results from supervisors, which also contributed to the delay.”

Mr Ravunawa said the ministry also had to deal with several appeals against recommendations made by the posting committee.

These processes resulted in the interns remaining at home for weeks before their placements were finally confirmed.

The delay had raised concerns about the prolonged absence of interns from hospitals, particularly rural facilities where medical staff are often stretched, and additional support is needed.

He said the interns could only be posted after the required academic, assessment and administrative processes had been completed.

He said the ministry had now finalised the postings, allowing the interns to begin their placements at rural hospitals and resume their clinical training and duties.

item.title: Court rules Vosanibola has case to answer
item.description: THE Suva Magistrate’s Court has ruled that former parliamentarian Peceli Vosanibola has a case to answer on corruption-related charges brought by FICAC. Magistrate Joseph Daurewa delivered the ruling yesterday, finding there was sufficient evidence on each element of the two offences for the matter to proceed to the defence stage.
item.content:encoded:
THE Suva Magistrate’s Court has ruled that former parliamentarian Peceli Vosanibola has a case to answer on corruption-related charges brought by FICAC.

Magistrate Joseph Daurewa delivered the ruling yesterday, finding there was sufficient evidence on each element of the two offences for the matter to proceed to the defence stage.

Mr Vosanibola is charged with one count of providing false information to a public servant and one count of obtaining a financial advantage.

It is alleged that on January 29, 2019, he falsely declared to the then acting secretary-general to Parliament, Viniana Namosimalua, that his permanent place of residence was Navuloa Village, Bureta, Ovalau.

FICAC further alleges that between August 1, 2019, and March 31, 2020, he obtained a financial advantage of $19,749.50 by submitting allowance claims while residing permanently in Nadera, Nasinu.

Following the ruling, the court advised Mr Vosanibola of his legal options, including his right to remain silent, give evidence, or call witnesses in his defence.

The matter was adjourned to August 28 for Mr Vosanibola to indicate how he intended to proceed.

item.title: Magistrate weighs sentencing options
item.description: A SUSPENDED sentence should not be viewed as an easy way out in domestic violence cases, Magistrate Yogesh Prasad warned as he considered a vegetable seller’s assault on his wife. On August 10, the 36-year-old man admitted in court to assaulting his wife following an argument after they returned from church.
item.content:encoded:
A SUSPENDED sentence should not be viewed as an easy way out in domestic violence cases, Magistrate Yogesh Prasad warned as he considered a vegetable seller’s assault on his wife.

On August 10, the 36-year-old man admitted in court to assaulting his wife following an argument after they returned from church.

The court heard he approached his wife while she was at home with their children and struck her with a stick, causing injuries to the right side of her face and the back of her neck.

The court heard there were financial difficulties in the relationship and that the victim had since moved and was not receiving financial support from the man.

Magistrate Prasad stressed the seriousness of domestic violence and the importance of punishment, noting that offenders could return to similar behaviour.

He said the circumstances of the offending had to be carefully considered and stressed the need to protect victims and ensure offenders understood the seriousness of their conduct.

Sentencing has been scheduled for September 1.
